questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Definetely the fact that I could study the German political system and situation, while at the same time improving my German language skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it has been a great experience overall. However, the process with choosing courses, getting them approved and getting accepted into classes by professors has been a little bit complicated.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the introduction days at Freie were great. However, the website with the course catalogue is quite confusing and I found it hard to figure out when and how to pick courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The introduction days were helpful. And you can also show up physically to get help from the Erasmus coordinators. Also, Freie were quite good at responding to emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think the system is a bit confusing for exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was ok - I found a WG with three roomies on WG gesucht. I think I was quite lucky.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are advantages, if you live in the middle of the city - the city is more available, where living on Campus is more outside the city. However, it did take me a while to get to Freie; 55 minutes from door to door.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't visit or try to get student housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it took a long time. However, I know that a lot of the registration is necessary.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It started back in November 2023, when we had to apply for a spot. Then, you get accepted, have to accept and apply for getting accepted at Freie Universität. Overall, the process has been ok, even though there are a lot of different online systems to be aware of.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always show up physically to get help or send an email. However, I think the online system is the confusing part.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think to show up physically and the Erasmus incoming office and get help with choosing courses. This was very helpful to me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I really liked my courses and found them interesting. Also, it was very nice to be able to choose courses from Sociological department or other departments at Freie Universität.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was fine - maybe not as difficulty as in Copenhagen. But overall, I liked the level - especially since I took half of my courses in German, I found the level to be quite fitting. However, I have heard that the exchange courses at Freie Universität are very easy and not difficult in terms of academic level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think the professors in general were less guiding/facilitating the classes. Often, they didn't present the texts, but started out with a class discussion. Therefore, the structure was a bit different compared to UCPH. Sometimes, students also had to be in charge of an entire class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Resilienz demokratischer Systeme (Resilience of democratic Systems)
Lecture Series: US Foreign Policy in Turbulent Times
Moderner Rechtsextremismus (Modern right-wing extremism)
Deutsche Außenpolitik seit 1945 (German foreign policy since 1945)
Intermediate Data Analysis and Visualization in R
Knowledge politics and economy of conflict and violence part 1 & 2

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you are interested in German politics (and have a sufficient German level), I would recommend: 
Deutsche Außenpolitik seit 1945 (German foreign policy since 1945)
It's a fun class with some work, but you learn a lot!

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay a semester fee at Freie. This, however, guarantees that you have free transportation in Berlin the entire semester, which is really great. You pay a little over 2000 DKK for the semester fee  - the free transportation is included in this fee.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Books. I didn't spend money on books at all. 
The 6-week language course BEFORE the start of the semester that Freie offers costs 5800 DKK. This can also be part of your budget.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are uni-sports just like at Copenhagen University. I didn't use the offer but it was great.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were multiple activities and events arranged for students. I have no complaints here.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend doing a 6 week language course before starting your studies - specifically the one that Freie offers. Even though it is a bit expensive, it is a really great way to get to know other exchange students and also improve your german.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Hamburger Bahnhof 
Gropius Bau
Tempelhofer Feld
Körner Park!! 
Hang out at: 
Helmhlotzplatz
Richardkiez
and discover Schöneberg - the area close to Nollendorfplatz!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: This was no problem!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Be part of a class that is taught in German. This was the way I got to know local Germans. 
Also, find housing through WG-gesucht. I got to live with three German students and really enjoyed this!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Speaking German in front of native german speakers. This was intimidating.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way people use bars, restaurants and green spaces in Berlin during the spring and summer period. Everyone is out on the streets, which I enjoyed a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Ask a lot of questions to Freie's Incoming Erasmus Team 
- Do a language course before hand if you want to improve your German
- Live off-campus and find your own place to live

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my German language skills. And meeting a lot of nice people!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing friends at home, and still studying when summer begins in Denmark

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I can definetely recommend spending a semester at Freie!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
